comment:
Good wings and footprint; keep the wings, their porticoes and colonnades, the footprint and the height. Fix the dome and the roofs:
1. The dome reads squat and stepped like a beehive. Rebuild it as Walter's dome: a tall round peristyle drum ringed by free-standing white columns (a continuous colonnade of 1-block quartz pillars with dark voids behind, standing proud of the drum on a round base), an attic band of small windows above it, then a TALL, smooth, bell-shaped dome (round in plan, about 12-13 across at its base, its profile rising steeply then curving in: use stairs and slabs for a smooth curve, white, with thin light-grey ribs running up it), a small colonnaded lantern (tholos) on top, and the dark bronze Statue of Freedom on it. The dome should be the tallest, most graceful thing, rising high above the wings (to about y 39). It should never look like a stepped pyramid.
2. The light wells in the wings show orange/sand floors from above: roof them over (flat light grey roofs or glass skylights with grey frames), no orange.
3. The green blocks on the roofs (the small green pavilions) read like stray copper: remove them or make them light grey roof lanterns.
4. Light the West Front and the dome's drum warmly at dusk (hidden floodlights), so the dome glows.
summary:
I rebuilt the dome above the attic as a tall bell. The wing skylights now have grey floors instead of glowstone, the two green cupolas are light grey roof lanterns, and hidden glowstone floodlights now light the drum colonnade and the West Front loggia.
Everything else is unchanged: wings, porticoes, colonnades, footprint and the lower dome. All changes are in parts/dome-upper.mjs, parts/dome-lower.mjs and parts/colonnades.mjs; make.sh rebuilt build.nbt.
Check: 0 floating blocks, 0 orphans. I rendered and looked at all sides and zoomed in on the dome from the north, east and west.
applied: Dome: I replaced the beehive shell with a new 10-course bell (y26..35) whose radius curves smoothly: about 6 (12 across) for three courses, then 5.85, 5.6, 5.2, 4.65, 3.95, 3.1 and 2.05 at the top. Each step in the profile is a slab on the outside and an upright stair inside, with corner-shaped stairs on the diagonals, so it reads as a curve and not a stepped pyramid.

Dome ribs: 12 thin polished_diorite ribs, set off the axes so none is doubled. Near the crown only every second rib continues, so the top doesn't turn into a grey cap. There is also a ring of 12 small dark windows at y29.

The tholos sits on top (diorite_wall posts round a glowing core at y36..37, a stair-edged cap at y38..39), with the dark bronze Statue of Freedom above it (pedestal y40, figure y41..42). The peristyle (free-standing quartz columns on the 16-across ring with dark voids behind, on the base) and the attic window band were already there and are kept.

Light wells: the skylight floor under the glass was glowstone, which read orange from above. It is now smooth_stone, so the skylights read grey under clear glass with their polished_andesite grey frames.
Green pavilions: the two copper cupolas are now light grey roof lanterns: a calcite drum with dark panes, a polished_andesite stair ring and a smooth_stone_slab cap.

Dusk light: glowstone is hidden in the entablature's underside over the void between the columns and the drum (under the attic, so it can't be seen from above). It lights the colonnade and the drum on top of the drum's existing lit windows. Glowstone is also hidden in the West Front loggia ceiling (x9 y11, z41..54).
skipped: Height: the statue's top is now y42 (it was y41), which is about 3 blocks above the 'about y39' you mentioned. I kept the extra courses so the bell could be tall and steep; it is still well under the y45 limit. Taking one course out of the shell would bring it back to y41.
At this size the top three courses of the shell still show small stair steps where the radius drops fastest. This is the nearest smooth curve I could get from whole blocks, stairs and slabs.
The palette report still flags light-on-light quartz trim on the wings. That was there before and you didn't mention it, so I left it.
